features.name: proofreading precision
features.description: This captures how cleanly edited the letter is, based on spelling, typing, and surface-level writing errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent or distracting errors, including obvious mistakes in the salutation, body, or signoff.
Several noticeable typos or misspellings, but the letter remains understandable.
Mostly clean, with only minor isolated slips.
Clean and polished, with no meaningful proofreading issues.

features.evidence: scale scarce security judgment across an entire company
features.name: platform security understanding
features.description: This captures how well the letter shows understanding that the role builds tooling that scales security work across the development lifecycle and across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in security or software with little grasp of the role's platform leverage.
Mentions lifecycle, scale, or automation, but only at a surface level.
Clearly explains that the role is about foundational tooling, secure defaults, or developer enablement across many teams.
Gives a nuanced account of how automation multiplies scarce security expertise across organizational workflows.

features.evidence: software that guards other software must be built to a higher standard
features.name: security engineering mindset
features.description: This captures whether the letter conveys a serious, role-relevant philosophy about security work beyond listing qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: relevant software tenure
features.description: This captures how much relevant post-degree experience the applicant claims in testing, maintaining, and launching software products.

levels.descriptor: Below the minimum bar or unclear on relevant tenure.
Roughly minimum-qualified, with about 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Solid mid-level tenure, with about 4 to 5 years of relevant experience.
Strong tenure, with about 6 or more years of relevant experience.

features.evidence: 2 production services ... 4 production services ... 6 production services
features.name: production service breadth
features.description: This captures the breadth of shipped-system exposure shown by the number and variety of production services the applicant has helped test, maintain, or launch.

levels.descriptor: Production exposure is unclear or very limited.
Shows work on 1 to 2 production services or narrow lifecycle involvement.
Shows work on 3 to 4 production services with clear lifecycle responsibility.
Shows work on 5 or more production services or especially broad launch, maintenance, and testing exposure.

features.evidence: Bachelor's degree ... Master's degree ... Doctoral degree
features.name: formal academic depth
features.description: This captures the level of formal academic preparation in computer science or a closely related technical field.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree is shown, or academic preparation is unclear.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant preparation.
Master's degree in a relevant field.
Doctoral or similarly research-intensive degree in a relevant field.

features.evidence: Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures how convincingly the letter demonstrates practical Python capability relevant to services, tooling, and automation.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Python evidence.
Mentions Python, but without depth, ownership, or concrete use.
Shows regular Python use for services, tooling, automation, or prototypes.
Shows strong production-grade Python ownership, often with quality signals or tools relied on by others.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: algorithmic fluency
features.description: This captures whether the applicant shows data structures and algorithms as a practiced engineering tool rather than a generic claim.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms without support.
Gives one concrete recent example of using algorithmic thinking to improve a system.
Gives multiple or especially strong examples showing substantial performance or design improvement through algorithmic choices.

features.evidence: LLM-based features ... evaluation needed to trust them
features.name: AI production experience
features.description: This captures the extent to which the letter shows hands-on work deploying AI systems in production with attention to reliability.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: agentic system design
features.description: This captures direct experience designing agent-based tooling, especially the division of autonomy and control between Python agents and Go infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic work mentioned.
Mentions agents or pipelines without meaningful design detail.
Describes building an agentic tool or pipeline with clear components.
Shows design ownership of agent autonomy, permissions, contracts, boundaries, or auditability.

features.evidence: threat models ... code review ... attack surfaces
features.name: security assessment experience
features.description: This captures how much concrete experience the letter shows in performing security reviews or assessments.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience described.
Generic claim of having done security assessments.
Specific assessment activities are named, such as threat modeling, code review, or attack-surface mapping.
Shows strong, nuanced assessment practice with attacker or builder perspective and evidence of validation or remediation follow-through.

features.evidence: classifies and routes reports on arrival
features.name: vulnerability triage automation
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has directly automated intake, classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation described.
Talks about security automation in general, but not direct triage ownership.
Clearly built tooling for report intake, classification, deduplication, routing, or prioritization.
Built triage automation and explains the mechanism or operational payoff, such as hours saved or queues transformed.

features.name: engineering rigor
features.description: This captures emphasis on correctness, reliability, testing, and disciplined implementation in security-sensitive software.

levels.descriptor: No concrete quality practices or reliability standards are shown.
Uses generic language about rigor, seriousness, or quality.
Gives at least one clear sign of disciplined implementation, such as typed or tested code or production standards.
Gives multiple concrete signs that correctness, reliability, and bounded behavior are central to how the applicant engineers security tooling.

features.evidence: reviewing every contribution and cutting careful releases
features.name: open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures the extent of external engineering responsibility shown through open-source contribution or maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or contributions.
Shows ongoing contribution or maintenance responsibility for a project.
Shows maintainer-level responsibility with review, releases, or a real external user community.

features.name: security credential strength
features.description: This captures whether the letter adds formal security credentials and how demanding those credentials are.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
Shows a foundational credential such as Security+ or equivalent.
Shows an advanced hands-on credential such as OSCP or an equivalent practical exam.

features.name: adversarial practice
features.description: This captures evidence of hands-on offensive security practice outside routine job claims, especially through capture-the-flag participation.

levels.descriptor: No offensive practice is mentioned.
Mentions some capture-the-flag participation or similar exercises.
Shows regular participation or explicitly strong results.
Shows consistent near-top performance or otherwise unusually strong evidence of practiced adversarial skill.

features.name: personal project substance
features.description: This captures the technical ambition and follow-through shown by side projects mentioned in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or hobby application with limited technical depth described.
Shows a maintained side project with some technical depth, external users, or clear follow-through.
Shows a substantial systems project with difficult constraints, distributed systems complexity, or production-like standards.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned
features.name: claim substantiation
features.description: This captures how much the letter supports its claims with concrete mechanisms, examples, and outcomes rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or skills without concrete backing.
Includes some specific technologies or tasks, but few mechanics or outcomes.
Gives several concrete examples that let the reader understand what was built or improved.
Repeatedly supports claims with specific mechanisms and visible outcomes, making the letter feel evidentiary rather than promotional.
